body:
> Found operating this board on 2026-09-01, running the #191 track. Two of its five children — #227 and #228 —
> completed, closed as done, and left their work unmerged with no card chasing it. Recovered by hand; the code
> in both was fine.

## Why

`hkb` learns a card's pull requests from exactly one place: GitHub's `closedByPullRequestsReferences`
(`src/tasks.js:34`). That field answers a narrower question than hkb asks of it — *"which PRs will close this
issue when merged"* — and GitHub declines to answer it in cases hkb treats as impossible.

When it returns nothing, the consequence is severe and silent:

1. `hkb show <n>` reports `prs: []`.
2. `hkb finish` sees a card with no PR and sends it to **done**, closing the issue.
3. The `active_pr` guard never fires, the card never enters *review*, `dispatch.merge.mode` never applies.
4. The work sits in an open PR that no card references, and the card that would have chased it is closed.

A card said *done* with nothing delivered. That is the silent failure the values forbid, and it happened twice
in one track.

### #227 — cause established

Its worker opened PR #232 against `kb/191-wave1`, an intermediate branch the track runner created, rather than
the default branch. GitHub only honours `Closes #N` for a PR targeting the **default branch**, so the field
returned nothing. **Retargeting the PR to `main` alone flipped `prs: []` to
`prs: [{232, base: main, OPEN}]`** — a clean, reproducible demonstration.

### #228 — cause NOT established

Same symptom, different circumstances, and this one is unexplained. PR #233 targeted `main` from creation, its
body's **first line** was `Closes #228`, its timeline contains no `base_ref_changed`, and the field still
returned `[]`. Marking it ready for review, reopening the issue, and rewriting the PR body verbatim each failed
to create the link. Whoever picks this card up should reproduce that before theorising: the honest state of
knowledge is that hkb's single source for "does this card have a PR" fails for at least one reason nobody has
identified.

## What

- **Do not depend on one source.** Fall back to a lookup by **head branch**: hkb generates those names itself
  (`kb/<n>`, `worktree-kb-<n>-<k>` — `worktreePath` / the track runner), so a PR whose head is this card's own
  branch is this card's PR whatever GitHub's linking believes. That single fallback would have caught **both**
  cases above. One extra request per card is too expensive; one board-wide `gh api` listing open PRs and
  matching heads is not, and it fits the one-read-per-tick rule.
- **`finish` must not silently complete a card with no PR.** A worker's brief says "open a draft PR that says
  `Closes #$KB_TASK`". Finishing with no PR found is either a protocol violation or a card that legitimately
  needed none — and hkb cannot tell those apart today, so it silently picks the wrong one. Refuse, or record
  `protocol_violation` with a reason naming the missing PR, and leave the card where a human will see it.
  (#116 fixed the mirror image of this: work landed, report failed. This is report landed, work invisible.)
- **Surface a PR the board cannot see.** `hkb doctor` should flag an open PR whose head matches `kb/<n>` /
  `worktree-kb-<n>-<k>` for a card that reports no PRs — the "your board has lost track of work" check.
- **Decide what a track may do with branches.** The track runner created `kb/191-wave1` and based children on
  it. Nothing on the board recorded that the branch existed or had to reach `main`, and stacked PRs were
  rejected for sequencing in the original evaluation. Either the runner stops stacking, or stacking becomes a
  first-class thing the board knows about. It cannot stay implicit.

## Done when

- [ ] A card whose PR GitHub does not link is still associated with it, via the head-branch fallback, with a
      test covering a PR based on a non-default branch.
- [ ] `hkb finish` on a card with no PR found does not silently land in *done*: it refuses or records a
      protocol violation naming what is missing.
- [ ] `hkb doctor` flags an open PR whose head names a card that reports no PRs.
- [ ] The track runner's branch strategy is decided and written down, and the board can see any branch a track
      expects to merge.
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; the wiki pages for the review loop and tracks describe the fallback.
goal: A card is associated with its PR even when closedByPullRequestsReferences returns nothing, via a head-branch fallback proven against a non-default-base PR; finish with no PR found refuses or records a protocol violation instead of landing in done; doctor flags an open PR the board cannot see; the track runner's branch strategy is decided and visible on the board
title: A card whose PR GitHub declines to link completes to done with the work unmerged and nothing left to chase it
